page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-48 is an x86_64 compute-focused virtual machine instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs and 90 GB of system memory. This hardware allocation yields a ratio of approximately 1.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, aligning it with compute-centric processing requirements. The server type does not bundle local NVMe or solid-state storage, necessitating network-attached persistent disks for data storage. In addition, it does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The instance architecture isolates resource expenditure primarily to processing throughput, minimizing unused memory overhead. For tasks with low memory requirements per processing thread, this dense compute allocation delivers qualitative resource efficiency compared to balanced or memory-optimized profiles. Operators must provision external storage performance independently, matching network-based disk input/output capabilities with operational requirements.

Given the high core count and reduced memory-per-core ratio, the c4d-highcpu-48 is engineered for compute-heavy processing rather than in-memory caching or massive databases. Suitable deployments include distributed continuous integration and compilation clusters, batch processing, media transcoding, scientific computing simulations, and high-throughput stateless web application serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-48 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. Configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 90 GB of system RAM, it maintains a ratio of 1.88 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage disks and does not contain discrete hardware accelerators, necessitating external network block storage for persistence. By allocating a high number of dedicated processing threads alongside a moderate memory footprint, the instance is engineered for computational workloads where substantial memory reserves are unnecessary. This design provides cost-effective compute capacity for compute-bound operations rather than memory-heavy systems. Practical workload deployments include software compilation, CI/CD runners, batch media transcoding, distributed processing nodes, and high-throughput stateless web application serving.
